10A.
Discussion regarding on-sale and off-sale alcohol establishments in the City of Encinitas. CASE NO: 16-311 POD; LOCATION: Citywide. Contact Person: Associate Planner Winter
1) Direct staff to initiate a Deemed Approved Ordinance and use the City of Ventura's Alcoholic Beverage Establishments Ordinance as a model ordinance but modify it to include the Commission's recommendations and to fit Encinitas. As part of the ordinance, clearly define "over concentration"; 2) Direct staff to develop definition(s) to distinguish bars from restaurants with alcohol service; 3) Direct staff to initiate a separate amendment application to amend the performance standards in the Encinitas Municipal Code related to noise and include the Downtown Encinitas Specific Plan and North 101 Corridor Specific Plan as part of the amendment application. The Commission recommended to use the City of San Clemente Ordinance as an example and/or other jurisdiction ordinance that has standards for specific time periods. The Commission also recommended to include specific standards related to ambient noise citywide; 4) Direct staff to draft an Entertainment License Ordinance that is modeled after the City of Carlsbadâ€™s Ordinance; 5) Direct staff to evaluate options for increased citation/penalty fees through the Code Enforcement Division; 6) Direct staff to evaluate and report back on peer cities limitations on engine idling and party bus ordinances; 7) Encourage the City Council Economic Development Subcommittee to expedite their effort in analyzing economic development needs and strategies in the downtown area; and 8) Direct staff to evaluate supplemental needs in the Code Enforcement Division in response to code enforcement demands in the City with the focus in the downtown area. The commission discussed queuing concerns and suggested to require patrons to queue on site. However, if not feasible due to limited space, queuing may be permitted within the public right-of-way subject to a permit approval from the City to ensure pedestrian access is provided and maintained. This standard should be included in the new ordinance. In addition, it was also suggested by staff and supported by the Commission that a 10 p.m. closing time for alcohol serving establishments should be the starting point of discussion with applicants with the potential to extend the hours with a phased approach. That approach would be vetted through the use permit application review process and by the Commission through their consideration of the facts, and ultimately their action taken on the use permit. The phased approach could also include an opportunity for a probationary period (nine months to a year) to allow operators to demonstrate use compatibility with surrounding uses and accountability as business operators.

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
